title: Decision Fatigue
hook: By 3pm you've made so many tiny choices that the big one gets whatever's left of your brain.
statement: The more decisions you make, the worse each one gets.
explainer: Every trivial choice uses up the same energy you need for pricing, hiring, and strategy. Turn the repeat ones into rules and save your brain for what matters.
sop: Track every decision you make for one full day.
Score your Energy 1 to 10 and count your total Decisions.
Find 3 daily decisions that add zero real value.
Turn each one into a rule, template, or default.
Make your highest-stakes calls in the first half of the day.
equation_example: Energy 8, Decisions 40. 8 ÷ 40 = 0.2. Higher means your decisions are still sharp. Lower means you've burned through your decision energy and every choice from here gets a little worse.
question: Name one decision you make every day that you could turn into a rule.
closing_statement: Every small decision spends energy you'll need later.
caption:
Principle Nº 134: Decision Fatigue

By 3pm you've made so many tiny choices that the big one gets whatever's left of your brain.

The more decisions you make, the worse each one gets.

Your turn: Name one decision you make every day that you could turn into a rule.
